html:
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake in central Taiwan on 21 September 1999, centred near the town of Jiji in Nantou County. It killed about 2,400 people and was the island's deadliest in a century. Taiwanese call it the 921 earthquake, from the date.

The Chelungpu Fault ruptured for about 100 km, lifting the ground by metres in places. Thousands of buildings fell, including apartment blocks that turned out to have been badly built, and landslides blocked rivers in the mountains.

Power cuts briefly stopped the chip factories of Hsinchu, including those of TSMC, and world prices for memory chips jumped, a sign of how much the global electronics industry already relied on Taiwan. After the quake Taiwan tightened its building codes. The disaster came the same year as the Izmit earthquake in Turkey, and joins a list of great Asian quakes on the chart, such as the Tangshan earthquake.
